camera.reason: Single 13MP autofocus main camera with no OIS; the second ring is an AI lens, not a real sensor.

performance.reason: Unisoc T7200 with 4GB RAM is fine for basics but slows with several apps open.

battery.reason: 5,000mAh gets through a full day; 10W charging takes hours.

build.reason: Plastic frame and back with no confirmed IP rating.

software.reason: ZTE has published no OS update promise for the A36.

value.reason: Cheapest in stock phone in the bracket at 27,000, with 4GB RAM, dual DTS speakers and a headphone jack.

availability.reason: In stock at PriceOye and on Daraz with official ZTE warranty, but ZTE has fewer service centres than bigger brands.

notes: Sold in some markets as the ZTE Blade A36. WhatMobile lists 32,999 and launch coverage cited an 18,999 introductory price; PriceOye's 26,999 is in stock on 2026-10-10. Daraz sellers list it from 29,999. No fingerprint reader. Weight (194g) is from third-party sites; sources conflict on an IP54 rating, so it is left out.
